title: Chord fix regresses the drag-interrupt swallow latch: Press_Anchor is emitted AFTER Right_Click, undoing was_dragging's latch (old handle_input ended TRUE, new code ends FALSE)
detail: Spec: mouse must preserve behavior EXACTLY. On a right+left chord while a draw drag is active, old code netted press_swallowed=TRUE (chord reset, then was_dragging latch); the new intent order (Right_Click latches, then Press_Anchor clears) nets FALSE, so the anchored later release click-selects where the old code suppressed it. Reachable via scripted/mixed-device frames (live mouse can't re-edge a held button); r1 was correct here — the fix-introduced Press_Anchor broke it.
recommended_fix: Emit Press_Anchor BETWEEN Cancel and Right_Click (Cancel -> Press_Anchor -> Right_Click) so the drag-interrupt latch lands last, matching the old chord-then-was_dragging order.

title: input_parity_pad_cursor's first boundary is vacuous: only the FINAL pad_node==0 is asserted, which a dropped/no-op first Dpad_Up also produces
detail: The comment promises 'first Dpad_Up lands on the LAST alive node (2)'. With no cursor, pad_step's first Dpad_Down lands on node 0 — so a regression that silently drops the Up frame still ends at pad_node==0 and passes. The pinned first-placement boundary (step -1 -> n-1, the edge-hunter finding) is unasserted.
recommended_fix: Assert the intermediate state: snapshot pad_node after frame 1 (== 2) as well as after frame 2 (== 0) — e.g. split into two scenarios or add a per-frame checkpoint to the parity driver.

title: Class-key surface hard-capped at One/Two (Key enum + poll + mapping) while the old handle_input's class loop was catalog-driven (ONE+i for every packet type)
detail: The old loop polled KeyboardKey(ONE+i) for every catalog packet type; the new Key enum stops at Two, so a third packet class would silently have no class key (Key(One+2) aliases .E but that case never reaches the loop). No live delta today (catalog has 2 types), but the transcription narrowed a catalog-driven surface with no guard — r1-missed.
recommended_fix: Add a compile-time assert (len(cat.packet_types) <= 2) near the Key roster, or extend Key/poll rows to the catalog maximum, so a third class fails loudly instead of silently losing its key.

title: Stale 'Emphasis'/'Set_Emphasis' labels for Cmd_Set_Weights survive the #55 rename in the parity harness's failure strings + comments
detail: The #55 terminology adoption renamed Cmd_Set_Emphasis -> Cmd_Set_Weights, but the parity test's failure renderer still prints 'Emphasis{...}' and the lane-fold comment says 'Set_Emphasis'. Cosmetic only, but misleading when reading a parity failure bundle against current command names.
recommended_fix: Rename the failure-string label to 'Weights{...}' (or 'Set_Weights{...}') and update the comment to 'Set_Weights'.
